title: Ethambutol
dek: An arabinosyltransferase inhibitor (EmbCAB) used as a companion while DST is pending and in some intensive phases. Optic neuropathy is the monitoring tax. DST is noisy; embB 306 is the genomic handle.
story: Ethambutol is bacteriostatic against replicating Mtb by blocking arabinogalactan assembly. It is the “guardrail” in 2HRZE: if undetected INH or RIF resistance is present, EMB reduces the chance of losing the remaining first-line drugs. Once DS is confirmed, WHO is comfortable dropping it in continuation.

Adult dose ~15 mg/kg; children ~20 mg/kg. The feared toxicity is retrobulbar optic neuropathy — colour vision, visual acuity. Counselling beats a late complaint of “can’t see red.” Renal impairment needs dose adjustment because EMB is cleared by the kidney.
embB M306 variants are the resistance hotspot; phenotypic EMB DST is historically fussy. Do not let either alone overrule a thoughtful report. See tb-embcab.
deep: 9-month DR recipes may still list E as a companion. Count it only if embB/grade says so.
TBM: poor CSF penetration. Pediatric TBM recipes often swap in ethionamide rather than relying on EMB.
Not a sterilizing drug. Not a TPT drug.

visual.caption: EMB points at arabinogalactan in the envelope. Host toxicity points at the optic nerve — a different organ, same month of therapy.
visual.annotation: Companion, not sterilizing star. Drop when DS is known, per regimen.
